Use case: precise-object-edit, polished game environment concept.
Asset type: LCS industrial apartment hallway concept, lower floor view A. ONE standalone landscape interior image, 3:2, no captions or collage.

Input roles: Image 1 is the PRIMARY ARCHITECTURAL EDIT TARGET, the actual lower-floor stair corridor looking west. Image 2 is its opposing native view: use only to understand this same plan. Image 3 is an approved bathroom concept: use ONLY its convincing worn materials and realistic environment-art finish, never its bathroom fixtures or domestic decoration.

Preserve image 1's camera, high 3.8 m ceiling, straight corridor, exact door and narrow end-window positions, overhead duct routes, concrete stair flight on the RIGHT rising away toward the west, its dark steel rails and the rectangular upper-floor opening. This corridor is about 10 m long and 3.4 m across including the stairs; keep its real broad industrial proportions. The workshop and bathroom doorways are on the LEFT. Do not make extra openings or extend it into a long institutional maze.

This was the circulation area of a former commercial/industrial telecom tower serving a roof communication array. It was abandoned and stripped of expensive equipment before two girls moved in. The hall has barely been domesticated. Its walls are PAINTED PLASTER: the lower half, to roughly 1.9 m, is very old desaturated NAVY BLUE oil paint; the upper half is aged BEIGE WHITE. Clearly read both colours, with a slightly imperfect horizontal paint boundary. Preserve the raw concrete ceiling and worn grey-brown industrial floor. Localized flaking, scuffs near corners and door handles, peeled paint exposing older coats/plaster, hand grime at usable heights and a few repair patches; no uniform black soot or apocalypse destruction. The wall along the stair follows the same lower-floor navy scheme; any tiny glimpse of the upstairs landing beyond the opening can have faded green.

Tell the telecom history mainly through what was REMOVED. On the left wall, replace the foreground blockout shelving with a broad pale unpainted rectangular cabinet/shelf footprint with rows of empty fixing holes, rust halos around surviving bolts, lighter protected wall, old bracket outlines and a few chipped filler plugs. These are flush wall scars, not new installed cupboards. Add a second smaller cabinet ghost farther along, interrupted by the actual doorway. Keep old galvanized conduits and surface electrical boxes, a small section of mostly empty cable tray near the ceiling, clipped/cut cable tails and one restrained hanging wire loop. Do not fill it with active telecom racks or valuable equipment.

A recessed technical access hatch in the LEFT wall has a thin steel rim and a small hinged door standing partly open. Inside is a shallow dusty cavity with a few old ceramic fuse holders, disconnected cables and screw terminals. Fit it between the existing doors without moving them. Other service boxes may be closed. A few faded, partly overpainted, time-worn utilitarian wall stencils only: "CABLE RISER" near a conduit route, "LINE 04" near an old cabinet mark. Small lettering and partial ghosts integrated into paint, never fresh graphic signs or brand logos.

Make the actual room doors look COMMERCIAL: plain worn steel fire/service door leaves, stout metal frames, exposed robust hinges, metal lever handles, lower kick plates and simple overhead closers. Maintain the existing open/ajar leaves and the openings. No wood-panel apartment doors. Change the domestic bowl sconces to sparse wired old caged oval incandescent bulkheads in the same useful lighting positions.

The beginning of temporary salvage storage is visible, improvised and slightly careless: ONE low cluster along the LEFT wall under the removed-shelf mark, comprising two battered empty transport cases, a shallow crate of miscellaneous metal brackets, one tied coil of thick cable and a couple of reclaimed flat boards leaned safely against the wall. A smaller carton near the far end. The expensive guts have been stripped out of these shells too. It reads "might need this later"; no professionally arranged workshop, no wall-to-wall hoard. Keep the entire walking strip, both door approaches and the stair treads open. Remove the decorative red runners, concert posters and home furnishing. Almost all wall area remains old building history. No characters.

Lighting: comfortably readable aged industrial interior, a few muted warm incandescent pools, cooler overcast light through the existing narrow end window, neutral beige whites and distinctly navy paint in shadow. No orange wash, no sunbeams, no new windows. Physically convincing matte paint, chipped steel, dull zinc, dusty cardboard, cable rubber, soft contact shadows and weight. Strong environmental art, realistic eye-height perspective faithful to image 1. No people, plants, flowers, wireless, LED/RGB, neon, LCD/flat displays, real brands, extra rooms, curtains, decorative art, captions, UI, arrows, borders or watermark.
